# Syllabus

**Instructor:** Scott Murff, Strategy Program Director\
**Teaching Assistants:** Sarah Millett and Luke Stacey, who also serve as Strategy Program co-presidents\
**Credits:** 1.5, letter graded\
**Semesters:** Fall and Winter\
**Class Time:** Fridays, 12:30 to 1:45 PM\
**Class Location:** 1315 TNRB\
**Office Hours:** Wednesdays 1:30 to 3:30 PM in 587 TNRB, Fridays 3:00 to 3:30 PM by phone\
**Note:** The last 30 minutes on Wednesday (3:00 to 3:30) are by phone as well

## Content Overview

Strategy Leadership Lab is a weekly working session for the roughly 30 students who lead the
BYU Strategy Program and the four career clubs it administers: MCA, PMA, CSA, and WSA. Those
clubs serve students across campus by career interest rather than by major, and the leadership
team reflects that: about half of the people in this room are majoring in something other than
strategy. It exists to do two things at once: develop you as a leader, and give the whole
leadership team protected time to coordinate on shared priorities.

The Lab is the primary coordination mechanism in the [Strategy Program operating
model](01-operating-model.qmd). One meeting cadence governs the entire program.

Enrollment is limited to program and club leaders and is open to them regardless of major. It
is optional but encouraged for everyone serving in a presidency. If your schedule prevents you from enrolling, you are welcome to audit
or simply attend.

## Weekly Structure

Each session runs in two blocks.

| Block | Minutes | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Leadership development | First 30 | Guest speakers, case discussions, skill building on influence, conflict, and managing up |
| Project roundtable | Last 45 | Club and presidency updates, cross-team coordination, peer feedback and coaching |

## Who Is in the Room

All student leaders across the program: the presidency (co-presidents, VP Events, VP Marketing),
the MCA, PMA, and CSA co-president pairs, the WSA co-presidents, VP Alumni, VP Student Development,
and club VPs. They come from a range of majors, and the clubs they run serve a student
population wider than the strategy major.

## Required Tools

Every student in the Lab maintains a paid AI subscription for the semester. Either one:

| Tool | Tier | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Pro | $20 per month |
| ChatGPT | Plus | $20 per month |

Claude Pro is the default and what the follow-along drills are built around. ChatGPT Plus is
an accepted substitute. Free tiers do not work for this course: the usage limits stop you
partway through a drill.

There is no AI exam. The subscription exists because you use it in class every week.

Bring a laptop every week. The Drills block is a live follow-along and the Practice block is
forty five minutes of working, so both require a machine and a working subscription.

If the subscription is a financial hardship, talk to Scott before the add/drop deadline
rather than dropping the course.

## Grading

The course is letter graded. Four components:

| Component | Weight |
|---|---|
| Weekly update emails | 40% |
| Attendance | 25% |
| Feedback conversations | 20% |
| Discussant | 15% |

Nothing is graded on hours worked, so an unpaid volunteer VP can earn full marks. See
[Assessments](00-assessments.qmd) for detail.

## Credit and Pay

Students do not receive pay and credit for the same work.

- Class is where you reflect, discuss, and learn. The job is where you execute, deliver, and
  coordinate.
- Student employees may not log paid work hours during scheduled class sessions or on
  class-specific assignments.

## Course Policies

Attendance, AI use, accommodations, and the standard BYU policy language: to be written.
